_says: The internal callers that may act for an account without a person's sign-in (src/service-actor.mjs). Each origin is a row naming the file that mints it and the kinds of scope it may mint: a new caller or a new kind of work is a new row here, not code. A service actor is minted by the account's own policy owner only (AccountControl mintServiceActor), as the principal service:<origin> with a proof only that owner can make (keyed BLAKE3 over the account, the origin, the time it was minted and its scope, with a key the owner generated for the account and never returns). Every account gate refuses a service: or system: principal whose proof its policy owner has not verified, so no request, header or forwarded claims object can stand as one. A gate opens for it only the gates its scope kind names (a gate row with resource_is_scope opens only the resource its scope id names; one with resource_prefix opens each resource whose address starts with it, such as an original-work affinity gate @affinity:<key>), with the operations named there, and, where a gate names a bound field, only for its own scope id. A gate row naming inputs for an operation admits that operation only with one of them exactly; one marked plan_free is work every account is given, which no plan withholds. The gate then decides it as it decides a sign-in: the reach its scope kind names at most, plan, budgets and stops, an ended principal, deletion, disconnection before its mint, and erasure.
_reserved_prefixes: Sign-ins with these prefixes are service principals: only a minted one with a verified proof stands. Minted actors are service:<origin>.

scope_kinds.says: One tool run of the account: describing and running its tool, and its run's own rights.

gates.says: Only the run it was minted for.
Describing and running the tool of its own run.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Reading the operator account's Brand assets list and worn Screen look, which every page and email draws.
scope_kinds._reach: The reach its gates already recorded for service:brand-presentation before it was minted: a different reach is refused there as a changed sign-in. Its operations are what narrow it.

gates.says: The Brand assets list and the looks routes.
Which records resource holds the Brand assets list (its original-work affinity), for that list read only.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: A visitor of a site the account installed, once the account's own records were carried to its own records book: the site's committed snapshot and Worker settings, its installation and public records, its page views, form answers and shop reads, asked of the account's own records (src/public-app-visitor-call.mjs). The installer's records check that each call names one of their own live installations.

gates.says: The visitor methods of one installation (src/public-app-visitor-call.mjs PUBLIC_APP_VISITOR_OPERATIONS), nothing else.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Another member's Sites call on a Space site the account installed, once the account's own records were carried to its own records book: the call is asked of the installer's own records in that member's name (src/account-app-state.mjs accountAppReply), which answer it as the installer's store did, the member's own Space access checked there (src/native-public-apps.mjs public-app:memberRequest).

gates.says: One member's Sites API call on one of the installer's Space sites, nothing else.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: The operator's one-time import of a retiring store's lists and rows into the account's own records: saving a list, putting its rows and reading them back.

gates.says: save_list, put_list_rows and read_list, import:records for the typed records the import names (src/import-record-types.json), and import:workspace-records for the workspace records it does not refuse (src/import-workspace-not-imported.json).
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: The operator's one-time carry of a retiring store's sealed saved-login box into the same account's live box (src/native-saved-logins-owner.mjs merge_archived): the scope id is the BLAKE3 identity of the one archived snapshot it carries, which that owner checks.

gates.says: Only its merge_archived body: the saved-logins owner refuses any other body from a service actor.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: A Namespace resource's own background work (its alarm and housekeeping), on that one resource of the account.
scope_kinds._id_pattern: The Namespace resources a Namespace book is ever mounted for. Every route to one (namespace-native-routing ensureNativeNamespace and routedNativeNamespaceHttp, namespace-native-command, account-native-move, and the resource-dependency:namespace record a book installs from its own resource) names @namespace; an independent Namespace has no creator in src (namespace-native-host createIndependentNamespace has no caller, and namespace-book-resource createIndependent refuses @namespace). The creator of an independent Namespace adds its resource format here.

gates.says: Only the Namespace resource it was minted for, and only its own lifecycle work.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Writing a showcase's seed DATA into the throwaway account the live host made for it.

gates.says: The showcase's files.
The activity rows the showcase names.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: What every new account is given when it is made, whatever its plan: its own directory profile (its relay and the names it signed up with) and its own community.

gates.says: Only filling its directory profile, publishing the profile that fill committed (profile:publish verifies its completed control intent) and reading its communities, which makes its own one: each admitted request's input is the one named, and no plan withholds them.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Keeping the names a purchase's checkout carries in the buyer's own directory profile, where the profile has none the person wrote.

gates.says: Only whether the profile still wants a purchase's names, keeping them (never over a name the person wrote), and publishing the profile that keep committed (profile:publish verifies its completed control intent); a buyer's own names are kept whatever their plan.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Reading the bytes the account's Namespace keeps, the one reading of its plan's daily usage count its policy owner cannot read itself.

gates.says: Only the Namespace summary read (src/account-plan-usage.mjs NAMESPACE_SUMMARY_URL), whatever the plan: a plan that charges by use is counted on every account it covers.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Starting the runs the account's own rules and schedules start when they fire, and reading those runs on: the account's rule authority, never a caller's.

gates.says: Starting a rule's or schedule's tool or workflow run, and reading its run on.
The same, for a rule or schedule of one of the account's own independent work resources.
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Handing one job of Trillion's own work (a failing watch, a stopped service check, a client health issue) to the AIs of the account that runs Trillion.

gates.says: hand_off, one job per episode (once_per).
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Telling the person of one account a notice from one of Trillion's own owners (a bill heading past its budget, everyone's model spend reaching its budget).

gates.says: One notice under its own key (src/tell-the-person.mjs keeps one notice per key).
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Ending one account's follow-up emails from the stop link they carry, when the link's token is that account's own.

gates.says: Ends them only for the token the account's own follow-ups keep (src/follow-up-emails.mjs stop).
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: The operator's one-time carry of a fenced store's Namespace into the same account's own Namespace book (src/carry-out.mjs carryOutNamespace, POST /mcp/api/storage/carry-out with part namespace).

gates.says: Only the Namespace carry's own pages, whatever the plan: the account's files carry as they are. The operator's restore work is paid by Trillion's service, never counted against the person's own daily cap (spend-meter.json plan-daily-cap).
Only reading and naming the published Namespace on the account's own records (src/namespace-book-resource.mjs carryStep).
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

scope_kinds.says: Taking one arrival a carrier brought for an account with no person's sign-in behind it (mail to the account's own address, and that mail when it is sent again from the edge).

gates.says: Only taking the arrival, under the account's plan as any carrier's is (src/standalone-resource-behavior.mjs inbound:take).
Its use is noted like any sign-in's.

_readers: Files that read what a service actor's scope row says (the origin of its claims, who pays for its work: src/service-actor.mjs serviceWorkPayer) and mint nothing. test/service-actor.test.mjs lets exactly these, and the files of the origin rows below, import src/service-actor.mjs.

origins.says: The payment owner prepares prospective resource prices through the service seller's own Workshop rules; payer fields never choose another seller.

A rule or schedule the person set up runs its tool or workflow when it fires, as the account's own rule actor its policy owner mints (src/standalone-resource-behavior.mjs ruleActor), never as a caller of the account's records.
Trillion's own watch runs the account's tools that start a deploy waiting for its restart window.
One of Trillion's own service checks runs a probe tool on the account's own connections.
A workflow step that runs a tool, on the run the person started.
A connection's own tool tells the person about a change in that connection.
The operator fulfils an access request the account made during setup.
The operator refreshes a device distribution source on its window.
The service reads the operator's brand to draw its pages and emails.
A site's visitor reaches the carried account that installed it: the site's snapshot and Worker settings, its installation and public records, page views, answers and shop.
A member edits a Space site whose installer's own records were carried: the call is asked of the installer's book in the member's name.
The operator imports a retiring store's lists and its sealed saved-login box into a named account (POST /mcp/api/storage/import).
A Namespace resource runs its alarm and housekeeping once it was activated by an admitted command.
The live host writes a showcase's seed DATA into its throwaway account.
Trillion reads the owner's own connected GitHub source project for one request: a pinned source build check, or a source project request the account makes to its own Sites.
A new account is given its own directory profile and community when it is made (src/worker.mjs accountMade).
A purchase's checkout names are kept in the buyer's own directory profile: by the payment notice as it arrives (src/payment.mjs) and by the operator's fill for purchases made before it did.
A policy owner counts its account's plan usage each day: the bytes its Namespace keeps, for a plan that charges by use.

The service's own watch, check, client health and community matching owners hand their work to the AIs of the account its service_work_setting names, through that account's own records (RecordBook handServiceWork).

Trillion's own owners (the service watch's bill notices, the model budget alert of everyone's spend) tell the person of the account a notice through that account's own records (RecordBook tellServiceNotice, src/service-notice.mjs).
The stop link of an account's follow-up emails ends them in that account's own records (RecordBook stopOwnFollowUps, src/worker.mjs).
The operator carries a fenced store's Namespace into its account's own Namespace book (POST /mcp/api/storage/carry-out).

The destination Namespace book's own alarm carries the Namespace on, in bulk, once the operator started it (POST /mcp/api/storage/carry-out with bulk start): the same carry as the operator's, driven from Cloudflare.
Mail to an account's own address, and that mail when the edge sends it again, is taken by the account's own records (src/inbound-mail.mjs, src/share-inbox.mjs).
